recipes.name: Bacon and Tomato Cups
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) can refrigerated buttermilk biscuit dough

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease 32 mini muffin cups or line with paper liners.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook bacon until evenly browned. Drain on paper towels, then crumble into a medium mixing bowl. Mix in tomato, onion, Swiss cheese, mayonnaise, and basil.
Separate biscuits into halves horizontally, then cut each piece in half again for 32 pieces. Roll slightly to flatten, then place each piece into a prepared muffin cup. Spoon bacon mixture over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 10 to 12 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon and Tomato Cups
raw_recipe.description: These little muffin cups baked with tomato, bacon, Swiss cheese, and buttermilk biscuit dough are savory bites of heaven you won't be able to resist.

review.reviewBody: For those of you who thought the biscuit dough was a little too heavy, the second time I made these I used the mini frozen phyllo dough cups and they were trememdous. I also cut way back on the mayo and still stuck with a good jar of brushetta in lieu of chopped tomato.

I just couldn’t see using a mini muffin pan for this recipe, so I used my regular size pan. The consensus among many reviewers was to cut back the mayo, so I cut it in half, and I’m glad I did. I used Pillsbury Grands Flaky Biscuits, and I’d recommend that you use a quality biscuit, as well (it’ll make a difference). FYI, after I fit each biscuit half into each muffin cup, I took the bottom of a small juice glass and pressed down, to be sure there’d be enough room for the filling. Baked for 14 minutes, and they popped right out of the pan, perfectly cooked. Very good breakfast this morning along with fresh fruit, and definitely will be made again, probably with a healthy shot of hot sauce next time.

These were a HUGE hit at a party I went to last night! They went so fast, I had so many people ask me for the recipe, and people even asked if I had more hidden away somewhere.

I did read through quite a few reviews and followed some of the modifications.

This is my recipe mod that made 45 bacon tomato cups:

Two cookie sheets of bacon (16-20 pieces) baked in the oven, blotted to remove fat, cooled and chopped......

8 oz of shredded swiss cheese......

2 chopped tomatoes......

2 tbsp of minced fresh basil......

1 yellow onion chopped and caramelized......

2/3 cup of mayo......

When everything is cooked and chopped, throw it together in a medium bowl. You can make this part ahead of time and refrigerate if you want.

When it's time to throw everything together, I preheated the oven to 375, put 45 small phyllo dough cups on a cookie sheet and then scooped the filling into each shell (a heaping amount).

Bake for 12-15 min.

These are the best savory, flaky, cheesy bacon-y appetizer I've made! Like I said before: they were such a hit!

After reading reviews, I did this a couple different ways with the biscuits...but first off for the filling. I used what I had on hand. I used 2 roma tomatoes, 1/3 cup bacon bits, cheddar cheese, and only 1/3 cup mayo. For the biscuits, I tried a few cut in half, some in 1/3 and some in 1/4. If you are going to use 1/2 a biscuit, I suggest you use a regular sized muffin pan, NOT a mini pan. If you cut the biscuit in 1/3 or 1/4, than go ahead and use the mini pan. Don't forget, the biscuits will rise! I like the 1/4 size. they are the perfect size for an appetizer/finger food. the 1/3 size is not too much bigger but not as "cute" as an appetizer. The 1/2 biscuit is more like an after school snack size, or alongside dinner. Will be making this again.

These were a hit.. following others' suggestions, I used phyllo shells instead of biscuit dough. I also used half the amount of mayonnaise. Because the shells are already cooked, I didn't want them to burn so I baked the filling in a glass casserole dish at the recommended temperature for about 5 minutes. Then I put them in the shells and baked for another 5 minutes.. Perfect!

I made these for a get together with my friends, and everyone loved them. 
I wasn't sure if I would have enough filling, so I increased the filling 50%, but doubled the amount of Swiss cheese . I also added fresh ground sea salt, fresh ground pepper, and some grated parmesan cheese. 
I used regular size muffin pans. I used one can of biscuits, pulled each biscuits in half, then stretch the biscuit to is came up about 3/4" on the sides, then filled.
I backed at 375 degrees for 14 minutes, so the bottom of the biscuit was golden brown. 
Next time I make this I'll add a clove of garlic to the filling and some romana choose for a little more flavor.

I made several changes to this recipe. After reading the input of other members who have made this, and a first epic failed attempt in working with biscuit dough (I don't cook much with dough), I started over with phyllo dough. I also reduced the amount of bacon to six slices, as what the recipe called for seemed as though it would be a bit overbearing, and increased the amount of tomato. Finally, as I am not a huge fan of mayo, I reduced the mayo by about 2/3 and supplemented with a pear champagne dressing. It turned out well, but I think I will continue to work on this as I felt the bacon still overwhelmed the flavor. Phyllo was DEFINITELY the way to go.

LOVE these! I took these to a friend's "Supper Club" & everyone raved over them & asked for the recipe! The only modifications I make are: use crescent rolls cut & divided to fit a 24-mini muffin pan; microwave bacon (covered by a paper towel to absorb grease & prevent splattering); use 2 large Roma tomatoes, de-seeded & chopped; chop 1/2 onion & saute in a little EVOO/butter. Oh, & I use MUCH less mayo -- maybe 1/4 cup -- just enough to get everything to barely hold together. These are fantabulous!! Allow AT LEAST 3 per person as an appetizer!

I have made these twice now as a dinner meal with a different variation each time. The first time I made them in full-sized muffin pans and placed a whole biscuit in each cup. I used doubled monterey jack instead of swiss. It was excellent!
The second time I made this, I used fresh basil from my garden (which required doubling the amount) and split the biscuits in half per each full-size muffin cup. I used a generous 4 oz. of mozzarella and extra thick bacon made very crispy. It was ABSOLUTELY AMAZING! My husband requested this be added to the regular rotation of meals, which is rare.

I thought these were really good, but as written, it's just too much dough for a mini-muffin tin, and too much mayo. I will cut the dough into thirds next time. I also followed others' advice and used less mayo (probably between 1/3 and 1/4 cup). I used my Pampered Chef mini tart presser/tamper, and it made each biscuit perfectly shaped, and easy to fill! Thanks for the recipe!

These were so quick and simple to make. I used the mini size biscuits as that was what I had in the fridge. I bake these full size in a regular muffin pan for 18 minutes. I used pepper jack cheese as I had no swiss and served straight from the oven. The base was nice and crisp, the topping was so good too. Thank you for sharing this recipe.
I use flaky biscuits. Separate the layers to get 3 sections from each biscuit. Cook as described in the recipe. Very light brown crust.
Fabulous! This is a tasty appetizer to bring to a get together or if having friends over! Super easy and who doesn’t love bacon!?! These are always a hit and there are never any leftovers! Enjoy!!!

I really enjoyed these. I cut the biscuits into quarters, as the recipe stated, and they seemed just right. Maybe some reviewers read it incorrectly and used halves? I did use a little less mayo, and grilled the onions first, just per my own taste.

Loved it! Made it last week for a neighborhood get together, and everyone asked me to bring them again this week. I had to divide the biscuits horizontally as well as cut in half to make the number of servings. Thats the only confusing part of the recipe.
